# backend

## Classes

### AppMethodRefusal

An App method's declared domain refusal. A handler throws it to decline a call;
the generated method boundary returns it as a typed
[AppMethodReply](#appmethodreply) instead of an execution failure. Its message
is caller-facing App copy, so it must not carry private data.

- `Error`

### appBackend

Invoke this App's admitted backend. The App defines its JSON request/result.

---

### appMethods

```ts
const appMethods: CapabilityContract<{
  call: Promise<WhistleJsonValue>;
}>;
```

Call one of this App's declared, typed methods through its host. Unlike
`appBackend`, the host knows which method is called, so it can apply the
method's declared effect.

---

### appBackendActorHeader

```ts
const appBackendActorHeader: "X-Agar-Actor-Id" = "X-Agar-Actor-Id";
```

The admitting host overwrites this header from its authenticated principal. App
request bodies and incoming browser headers never supply this identity.

---

### appBackendComputerHeader

```ts
const appBackendComputerHeader: "X-Agar-Computer-Id" = "X-Agar-Computer-Id";
```

The admitting host overwrites this header with the Computer it has verified the
caller is admitted to use for this invocation, or omits it when no Computer is
bound to the call. App request bodies and incoming browser headers never supply
this identity: a backend that needs a Computer scope must read it from here,
never from its own request body.

---

### appMethodRefusalCodes

```ts
const appMethodRefusalCodes: readonly [
  "invalid",
  "forbidden",
  "not_found",
  "conflict",
  "unavailable",
];
```

The closed vocabulary an App method may refuse with. Each code names one
caller-visible outcome; the host owns how it is presented (see
[appMethodRefusalStatus](#appmethodrefusalstatus)).

### appMethodReplySchema

```ts
const appMethodReplySchema: ZodLazy<
  ZodDiscriminatedUnion<
    [
      ZodObject<
        {
          kind: ZodLiteral<"ok">;
          value: ZodJSONSchema;
        },
        $strict
      >,
      ZodLazy<
        ZodObject<
          {
            kind: ZodLiteral<"refused">;
            code: ZodEnum<{
              unavailable: "unavailable";
              invalid: "invalid";
              conflict: "conflict";
              forbidden: "forbidden";
              not_found: "not_found";
            }>;
            message: ZodString;
          },
          $strict
        >
      >,
    ],
    "kind"
  >
>;
```

Every generated App method RPC answers with exactly one of these.
